text.name: PowerShell script logging
text.titlePass: PowerShell records the scripts it runs
text.titleFail: PowerShell does not record the scripts it runs
text.why: Attackers do much of their work in PowerShell. Without this record nobody can tell afterwards what was run.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging" under Windows Components > Windows PowerShell.

text.name: Command lines in the security log
text.titlePass: The security log records how programs were started
text.titleFail: The security log does not record how programs were started
text.why: Knowing that a program ran says little; its command line shows what it was told to do. Investigations depend on it.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Include command line in process creation events" under System > Audit Process Creation.

registry.item: Command line in process creation events

text.name: Security log size
text.titlePass: The security log is large enough
text.titleFail: The security log is small
text.why: A small security log overwrites itself within days. By the time a break-in is noticed, its traces are gone.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open Event Viewer, right-click Windows Logs > Security > Properties and set the maximum size to 196608 KB.

text.name: Audit: sign-ins
text.titlePass: Sign-ins and failed sign-ins are recorded
text.titleFail: Sign-ins are not fully recorded
text.why: The record of who signed in, and of failed attempts, is how password guessing and stolen accounts are noticed.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Logon/Logoff > Audit Logon, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: account lockouts
text.titlePass: Account lockouts are recorded
text.titleFail: Account lockouts are not recorded
text.why: A lockout is the clearest sign that someone is guessing a password. Unrecorded, it goes unnoticed.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Logon/Logoff > Audit Account Lockout, with Failure.

text.name: Audit: programs started
text.titlePass: Every program start is recorded
text.titleFail: Program starts are not recorded
text.why: The list of programs that ran is the backbone of any investigation after a break-in.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Detailed Tracking > Audit Process Creation, with Success.

text.name: Audit: changes to auditing
text.titlePass: Changes to the audit settings are recorded
text.titleFail: Changes to the audit settings are not recorded
text.why: An intruder's first move is often to switch logging off. This records that it happened.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Policy Change > Audit Audit Policy Change, with Success.

text.name: Audit: password checks
text.titlePass: Password checks for local accounts are recorded
text.titleFail: Password checks for local accounts are not fully recorded
text.why: Each check of a local account's password, right or wrong, shows who is trying to get in and how often.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Account Logon > Audit Credential Validation, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: account changes
text.titlePass: Changes to user accounts are recorded
text.titleFail: Changes to user accounts are not fully recorded
text.why: New accounts and password resets nobody asked for are a common trace of an intruder making sure of a way back in.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Account Management > Audit User Account Management, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: group changes
text.titlePass: Changes to security groups are recorded
text.titleFail: Changes to security groups are not recorded
text.why: Being added to the Administrators group is how an intruder takes over a PC. This records who was added, and by whom.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Account Management > Audit Security Group Management, with Success.

text.name: Audit: devices plugged in
text.titlePass: Plugged-in devices are recorded
text.titleFail: Plugged-in devices are not recorded
text.why: A record of each device connected shows when a USB drive or other hardware was attached, for example to copy data off.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Detailed Tracking > Audit PNP Activity, with Success.

text.name: Audit: group membership at sign-in
text.titlePass: Group memberships at each sign-in are recorded
text.titleFail: Group memberships at sign-in are not recorded
text.why: The groups a user held at sign-in show when an account suddenly had more rights than usual.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Logon/Logoff > Audit Group Membership, with Success.

text.name: Audit: locks and reconnections
text.titlePass: Locks, unlocks and remote reconnections are recorded
text.titleFail: Locks, unlocks and remote reconnections are not recorded
text.why: These events show when the screen was unlocked and when remote sessions came and went, filling gaps in the sign-in record.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Logon/Logoff > Audit Other Logon/Logoff Events, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: administrator sign-ins
text.titlePass: Sign-ins with administrator rights are recorded
text.titleFail: Sign-ins with administrator rights are not recorded
text.why: Each sign-in that receives powerful rights is flagged, so misuse of an administrator account stands out.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Logon/Logoff > Audit Special Logon, with Success.

text.name: Audit: refused access to shared files
text.titlePass: Refused access to shared files is recorded
text.titleFail: Refused access to shared files is not recorded
text.why: Refused attempts on shared files show someone searching this PC's shares for what they may not open.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Object Access > Audit Detailed File Share, with Failure.

text.name: Audit: access to shared folders
text.titlePass: Access to shared folders is recorded
text.titleFail: Access to shared folders is not recorded
text.why: Connections to this PC's shared folders, and refusals, show who reached its files over the network.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Object Access > Audit File Share, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: scheduled tasks
text.titlePass: Changes to scheduled tasks are recorded
text.titleFail: Changes to scheduled tasks are not recorded
text.why: Malware often creates a scheduled task to start again later. This records tasks being created, changed or removed.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Object Access > Audit Other Object Access Events, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: files on USB drives
text.titlePass: File access on USB drives is recorded
text.titleFail: File access on USB drives is not recorded
text.why: Recording reads and writes on removable drives shows what was copied to or from them.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Object Access > Audit Removable Storage, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: changes to sign-in policy
text.titlePass: Changes to sign-in and trust policy are recorded
text.titleFail: Changes to sign-in and trust policy are not recorded
text.why: An intruder may grant rights or weaken sign-in rules to keep access. This records such changes.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Policy Change > Audit Authentication Policy Change, with Success.

text.name: Audit: firewall rule changes
text.titlePass: Changes to firewall rules are recorded
text.titleFail: Changes to firewall rules are not recorded
text.why: Malware often opens the firewall for itself. This records each rule added, changed or removed.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Policy Change > Audit MPSSVC Rule-Level Policy Change, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: failed policy changes
text.titlePass: Failed security policy changes are recorded
text.titleFail: Failed security policy changes are not recorded
text.why: Failures here include errors applying security policy and handling protected keys, which can be the trace of tampering.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Policy Change > Audit Other Policy Change Events, with Failure.

text.name: Audit: use of powerful rights
text.titlePass: Use of powerful rights is recorded
text.titleFail: Use of powerful rights is not recorded
text.why: Rights such as debugging other programs or taking ownership of files are what attackers reach for. This records each use.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > Privilege Use > Audit Sensitive Privilege Use, with Success.

text.name: Audit: firewall service and keys
text.titlePass: Firewall service and key storage events are recorded
text.titleFail: Firewall service and key storage events are not recorded
text.why: This records the firewall service stopping or failing, and problems with stored encryption keys.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > System > Audit Other System Events, with Success and Failure.

text.name: Audit: start-up, shutdown and clock
text.titlePass: Start-up, shutdown and clock changes are recorded
text.titleFail: Start-up, shutdown and clock changes are not recorded
text.why: A gap in the record or a changed clock can hide activity. This records when Windows started and stopped and when its time was changed.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > System > Audit Security State Change, with Success.

text.name: Audit: new services
text.titlePass: New services and security add-ins are recorded
text.titleFail: New services and security add-ins are not recorded
text.why: Installing a service is a common way for malware to start with every boot. This records each one installed.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > System > Audit Security System Extension, with Success.

text.name: Audit: system integrity
text.titlePass: Tampering with Windows' security checks is recorded
text.titleFail: Tampering with Windows' security checks is not recorded
text.why: This records failed integrity checks and lost audit events, which can be the trace of an attacker tampering with Windows.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The setting is Advanced Audit Policy > System > Audit System Integrity, with Success and Failure.
